draft.caption:
A drone strike, a quiet apology and a fight over the pace of AI 🌍🤖

BBC reports that a Russian drone struck a train near the Ukraine-Poland border, with no casualties reported. It hit shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials left the area, and BBC frames it as something that could mark an escalation.

France expressed regret for a post from a French official social media account that mocked the United States over a human rights vote. The regret came after the Trump administration blocked a new ambassador to Washington.

US tech leaders have called for pacing on AI, meaning a voluntary slowdown in development. Chinese researchers and state media pushed back, questioning whether the proposal is a genuine push for responsibility or an effort to entrench America's technological lead.

A jury was discharged in the Boris Johnson wedding plot trial after it failed to reach a verdict. Tim Speers was accused of planning a protest at the event.

A second federal judge moved to block a new US Postal Service rule that would tighten mail-in voting requirements. The US Supreme Court is still weighing the administration's request to overturn a separate order.

If the people in front call for a slowdown, is that responsibility or protection? 🤔

Source: BBC, NYT, SCMP

facts.title: Trump says AI safety fears a 'hoax' as he rejects calls for greater safeguards
facts.summary: The US president's comments come after Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark told the BBC an AI "kill switch" may need to be mandatory.
facts.article_excerpt: To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser. This video can not be played Watch: Great or alarming - Should AI be reined in? US President Donald Trump has said fears about the safety of AI are a hoax , as he criticised calls to have more guardrails for the fast-moving technology. It comes after Jack Clark, a co-founder of AI giant Anthropic, told the BBC that a kill switch for dangerous AI that can be checked by a third party may need to be mandatory for the industry. Clark's comments followed warnings about the risks the technology poses to humanity that have been raised in recent days by several executives and staff at leading AI firms. Those concerns triggered a selloff in shares of some tech firms on Monday as investors weighed the impact of a potential slowdown in the development of AI. In a series of social media posts on Monday, the US president compared warnings about AI to the Global Warming Scam , that he said was being perpetrated by the Radical Left Dumocrats . Trump also called himself the Hoax Buster , likening concerns about the safety of the technology to what he called the RUSSIA, RUSSIA, RUSSIA HOAX . In another post he wrote: There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China. WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! And earlier on Monday, Trump posted on social media that the only guardrails needed for AI was a strong and smart president. Also on Monday, Chinese state media said experts had warned that Washington's growing anxiety over China's rapid AI development appears to be increasingly distorting its policy priorities . They know that China has become a strong competitor in AI, and worry that if the US slows down development or tightens regulation, China could catch up even faster, Xin Qiang, a professor of American Studies at Fudan University, told the Global Times. Clark, who is one of Anthropic's seven founders, said earlier on Monday that a way of shutting off AI software completely if it gets too dangerous was something society might want to eventually pass rules around . He added that most labs have different ways of being able to pull the plug , including Anthropic, but said lawmakers may need to enforce having one. draft.headline: Trump calls AI safety fears a hoax, rejects new rules
draft.caption:
US President Donald Trump says fears about AI safety are a hoax, and he does not want more rules for the technology. 🇺🇸🤖

This follows Jack Clark, a co-founder of the AI company Anthropic, telling the BBC that a kill switch, an off switch, may need to be mandatory and checkable by an outside party. Clark said most labs already have ways to pull the plug, including Anthropic. He said lawmakers may need to enforce having one.

"There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China. WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS!"

Trump also posted that the only guardrails AI needs are a strong and smart president. He compared the warnings to what he called the Global Warming Scam. Chinese state media quoted experts saying US anxiety over China's AI progress is distorting Washington's policy priorities.

Warnings from executives and staff at leading AI firms in recent days helped trigger a selloff in some tech shares on Monday. What is still unsettled is whether any rule gets written, and who would hold that off switch.

Clark says an off switch may need to be mandatory because the technology keeps getting more powerful; Trump says slowing down is a conspiracy that only helps China. Which side are you on? 🤔

facts.title: Denmark says Russian warship fired flares at military helicopter
facts.summary: The Danish prime minister has accused Russia of "reckless" behaviour, while the Kremlin is yet to comment.
facts.article_excerpt: Image source, Rune Dyrholm / Danish Armed Forces By Henry Moore Published 46 minutes ago Denmark has accused a Russian warship of firing two emergency flares at one of its helicopters while it was tracking the vessel in the Baltic Sea. The Danish government has summoned the Russian ambassador over the incident, which it said happened during a routine monitoring operation on Monday. Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen branded the Russian action reckless and said it was designed to intimidate and divide . Moscow has not commented on the incident. It came on the same day Nato forces shot down a drone over Lithuania in the latest security scare on the alliance's eastern flank, where tensions remain high during Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. In a statement detailing the incident in the Baltic Sea, the Danish armed forces said: One of the air force's Fennec helicopters was today fired at with flares during a routine photographic operation of a Russian frigate, which was located in international waters off Gedser. Of the two flares fired at the helicopter, one passed close to it, the statement added. The Danish foreign ministry described the incident as completely unacceptable . Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen accused Russia of gradually shifting the boundary for what they consider acceptable behaviour , adding: That is something we cannot accept. Overnight, Nato fighter pilots shot down a drone that entered Lithuania's airspace. Authorities said the drone likely entered southern Lithuania, near the second-largest city of Kaunas, from neighbouring Belarus shortly after midnight on Tuesday. The origins of the drone are yet to be determined, the Lithuanian national crisis management centre said, but the country's president pointed to increased Russian aggression in recent months. President Gitanas Nausėda wrote on X: With Russia intensifying its aggression against Ukraine, such readiness is vital for our region. Together with our Nato Allies, Lithuania will defend its airspace. Lithuania shares a large part of its southern and eastern border with Belarus, a key Russian ally. Poland also announced there had been aviation operations in its airspace on Monday night due to the activity of Russian Federation's jet-powered unmanned aerial vehicles conducting strikes on Ukrainian territory . facts.title: Supreme Court blocks Trump's plan to restrict mail-in ballots
facts.summary: The Trump administration had asked the court to lift a federal judge's temporary block on new rules for mail-in ballots.
facts.article_excerpt: Image source, Getty Images By Lisa Lambert , Washington and Kwasi Gyamfi Asiedu Published 15 September 2026, 00:55 BST Updated 8 hours ago The US Supreme Court has rejected President Donald Trump's plan to restrict voting by mail before November's midterm elections, in a setback for the White House. The justices upheld a federal judge's order that temporarily blocked the US Postal Service (USPS) from moving forwards with new requirements for postal ballots. But it is unlikely to be the final word on the matter. Justice Brett Kavanaugh, a conservative, agreed with the ruling, but indicated he might later rule in Trump's favour as litigation in the case continues. Trump, who argued the rules would combat electoral fraud, signed an executive order in March directing the USPS to deliver ballots only to voters on lists of citizens. Legal challenges argued that the move violated states' constitutional rights to run elections. Justice Kavanaugh wrote in the opinion that there was at least a fair prospect that the final rule falls within the Postal Service's statutory authority . But he argued that applying the rule in the 2026 elections would be arbitrary and capricious . Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas, also conservatives, dissented. They wrote that the challenge to Trump's order was a Hail Mary pass that was unlikely to be successful ultimately. The Postal Service has broad authority to regulate the mail, they added. Trump signs executive order attempting to change mail-in voting Published 2 April Supreme Court allows late-arriving mail-in ballots in defeat for Trump Published 29 June The White House did not immediately comment on the decision. About 30% of voters, mostly Democrats, cast postal ballots in the general election two years ago. Since returning to the White House, Trump has sought to restrict voting by mail. While he himself has voted by post, he has long claimed this method allows non-citizens to cast ballots and is prone to fraud. In March's executive order, the president directed USPS to introduce unique barcodes on postal ballot envelopes. State and local election officials would also be required to supply information to an online portal about voters who receive mail ballots. Twenty-three states and Washington DC sued to stop Trump's order. The postal workers' union also said clerks could not be trained in time for the election. The justices upheld a federal judge's order that temporarily blocked the US Postal Service from moving ahead with new requirements for postal ballots.

"Arbitrary and capricious" is how Justice Brett Kavanaugh described applying the rule in the 2026 elections, even as he agreed the challenge might not win in the end.

Here is the part that is not settled. Kavanaugh also wrote there is at least a fair prospect the rule falls within the Postal Service's authority, and he signalled he might rule in Trump's favour later as the case continues. The White House did not immediately comment.

美國最高法院擋下川普限制郵寄投票的計畫。

大法官維持聯邦法官的暫時禁令,郵局在十一月期中選舉前不能推行郵寄選票新規定。川普三月簽了行政命令,要郵局只把選票寄給公民名單上的選民,信封還要加上專屬條碼。二十三個州加上華盛頓特區告上法院。

保守派大法官 Kavanaugh 站在多數這邊,但他寫說這規定有相當機會本來就在郵局的法定職權內,只是套到 2026 年的選舉太過武斷。Alito 和 Thomas 不同意,說這場挑戰只是撐不到最後的孤注一擲。

兩年前的大選,約三成選民用郵寄投票,多數是民主黨人。這件事還沒到最終定論。

美國最高法院擋下川普限制郵寄投票的新規定,十一月期中選舉前不能實施。最意外的一點:投下同意票的保守派大法官 Kavanaugh,同時暗示案子繼續打下去,他之後可能改站川普那邊。

#郵寄投票
被擋下來的是什麼?川普三月簽的行政命令,要郵局只把選票寄給公民名單上的選民,郵寄選票信封要加專屬條碼,州和地方選務人員還得把「誰收到郵寄選票」的資料上傳到一個線上系統。他的理由是防止選舉舞弊。二十三個州和華盛頓特區直接告上法院,主張這侵犯了各州辦選舉的憲法權力。
這件事影響多少人:兩年前的大選,約三成選民用郵寄投票,多數是民主黨人。郵務人員工會也說,選前根本來不及把窗口人員訓練好。白宮目前沒有回應這個裁定。順帶一提,川普自己也曾經用郵寄投票,但他長期主張這種方式讓非公民有機會投票、容易舞弊。

兩邊的理由都值得聽。Kavanaugh 認為規定本身可能合法,但在 2026 年選舉才改遊戲規則太過武斷。Alito 和 Thomas 反對,他們說郵局本來就有廣泛管理郵件的權力,這場挑戰最後撐不住。同一份規定,一邊看到的是時間點的問題,一邊看到的是權限從頭到尾都在郵局手上。你覺得哪一邊比較站得住腳?
